world_art_prompt.scene: Key art of the fantasy world 'Cup Product Gardens' at twilight, high three-quarter aerial view: terraced signal gardens of blue-gray stone where rows of tall lantern posts stand beside the paths; the lanterns glow gold in pairs and their beams cross and multiply into brighter points where they meet. Pools reflect the paths backwards like mirror images. In the distance, a long coastal reach where the land mirrors itself across a glowing seam — 'Poincaré Reach' — with matched towers on opposite sides. Further still, a rail station with a fake façade of a torus, its back side showing a different structure. Gyroid walks a garden path with a glowing gold chalice of light. A tall violet-and-red masked figure hides behind the station façade.

art.prompt: Terraced signal gardens with paired gold lanterns whose beams multiply; mirror pools; Poincaré Reach mirrored across a seam; the Counterfeit Station's torus façade; Gyroid with a gold chalice.

map.note: World 3 overworld layout (map units). Sites are places; paths are routes; gates need earlier tools.

sites.name: Garden Gate
sites.note: Where the delta's canals end in a garden stair.

gate.note: A hedge-wall of tiles: cut it to its boundary.
A lantern lock: light two lanterns whose product is the key.
The cliffs' stair lies on the orientation double cover: climb it with the Sheet Compass.

3-1.site: Mirror Pools — still pools that reflect every garden path backwards.
3-1.story: In the Gardens, the gardeners don't walk paths — they read them. A cochain is a reading: it assigns a value to every edge (or triangle). Its coboundary reads a triangle by reading its edges. The mirror pools show the delta's chains reversed: what was a boundary is now a coboundary.
3-1.objective: Assign readings to edges and triangles and compute coboundaries.
mechanics: Reading wand: set a value from a coefficient group G on every edge of a garden patch (a 1-cochain).
Coboundary: the pool shows the reading of each triangle as the signed sum of its edges' readings (δφ = φ∘∂).
δδ = 0 again, mirrored from 2-2.
Cocycles (δφ = 0) modulo coboundaries give cohomology classes.
3-1.math_check: Cochains Cⁿ(X; G) = Hom(Cₙ(X), G), δ dual to ∂, δδ = 0, Hⁿ(X; G) = ker δ / im δ (Hatcher pp. 190–197).

stages.name: Read an Edge
stages.description: Give each edge a value; the pool reads triangles from their edges.

stages.name: Balanced Readings
stages.description: Find readings with every triangle reading zero: cocycles.

stages.name: Readings from Points
stages.description: Readings that come from vertex values (differences) are coboundaries — they don't count.

stages.name: Around the Hole
stages.description: On an annulus, find a cocycle that isn't a coboundary: it reads 1 around the hole.

enemies.name: Echo
enemies.description: New: a violet reflection that mirrors Gyroid's moves with signs flipped; lash it in the pool, not on land.

3-1.tools: Unlocks the reading wand (part of the Boundary Blade's hilt).
3-1.music: Cup Product Gardens theme: a gentle 76 bpm waltz in F major, celesta and soft strings — first statement, with the melody sometimes played retrograde.
3-1.visuals: Twilight gardens of stone paths with still mirror pools reflecting them; gold values glowing on edges; reflected arrows pointing the opposite way.

3-2.site: Torsion Terrace — a terrace where twisted vines climb from one level to the next.
3-2.story: Cohomology is determined by homology — but torsion climbs up one floor. The projective plane's twisted loop (2-7) shows up in cohomology one dimension higher.
3-2.objective: Predict cohomology from homology using the Universal Coefficient rule.
mechanics: Terrace levels hold homology groups from Chain Delta.
Free parts stay on their own terrace; torsion vines climb to the next terrace (Ext).
Coefficient switch: with ℤ₂ readings the vines behave differently.
3-2.math_check: The universal coefficient theorem Hⁿ(X; G) ≅ Hom(Hₙ(X), G) ⊕ Ext(Hₙ₋₁(X), G); cohomology of RP², lens spaces (Hatcher pp. 190–206).

stages.name: Free Floors
stages.description: Torus: cohomology matches homology terrace for terrace.

stages.name: The Climbing Vine
stages.description: RP²: H₁ = ℤ₂ climbs to H² = ℤ₂.

stages.name: Change the Soil
stages.description: With ℤ₂ coefficients RP² reads ℤ₂ on every terrace.

stages.name: Plan the Terrace
stages.description: Predict cohomology for a lens space before reading it.

enemies.name: Vine choker
enemies.description: New: a violet vine that pulls torsion back down; two lashes.

3-2.tools: Uses the reading wand and the Mod Mill switch (2-9).
3-2.music: Gardens theme with a rising sequence each time a vine climbs.
3-2.visuals: Stacked stone terraces with twisted glowing gold vines climbing from each level to the next.

3-3.site: Lantern Rows — rows of lantern posts, each lantern lit by a reading.
3-3.story: Two readings can multiply: read a triangle's front edge with one and its back edge with the other. Gyroid forges the Cup Caster, which pours two lanterns into one — and swapping their order may flip the sign.
3-3.objective: Multiply cochains with the Cup Caster and learn the sign rule.
mechanics: Cup Caster (new): pick two lit lanterns (cochains φ, ψ); on each triangle, the product reads φ on the front face and ψ on the back face.
Coboundary rule: δ(φ ⌣ ψ) = δφ ⌣ ψ ± φ ⌣ δψ — products of cocycles are cocycles; products with coboundaries are coboundaries.
Graded commutativity: swapping two degree-1 lanterns flips the sign.
3-3.math_check: The cup product on simplicial/singular cochains, the coboundary formula, the induced product on cohomology, graded commutativity αβ = (−1)ᵏˡ βα (Hatcher pp. 206–212; graded commutativity p. 215).

stages.name: Front and Back
stages.description: Cup two edge readings on a single triangle.

stages.name: Products of Cocycles
stages.description: Cup two cocycles: the product is a cocycle.

stages.name: Swap
stages.description: Swap the order of two degree-1 lanterns: the light inverts.

stages.name: Light the Row
stages.description: Light a target lantern on a torus as a product of two.

enemies.name: Moth swarm
enemies.description: New: violet moths that put lanterns out; one lash each.

3-3.music: Gardens theme in two voices that multiply into chords when a cup is cast.
3-3.visuals: Rows of tall stone lantern posts at twilight; two gold beams crossing and pooling into a brighter third lantern; a gold chalice in Gyroid's hands.

3-4.site: Twin Islands — Null's two islands from the end of World 2, the torus and the two-loops-plus-sphere, side by side.
3-4.story: Null's World 2 claim: the torus and S¹ ∨ S¹ ∨ S² are the same place — their holes match. The Cup Caster tells them apart: on the torus, the two loop readings multiply to the top class. On the bouquet, their product is zero.
3-4.objective: Refute Null's World 2 claim with a nonzero cup product.
mechanics: Light the two degree-1 lanterns on each island.
Cup them: on the torus the top lantern lights; on the bouquet it stays dark.
Since cup products are preserved by homotopy equivalence, the islands aren't the same place.
3-4.math_check: Cohomology rings of T² and S¹ ∨ S¹ ∨ S²: same groups, different products; the ring is a homotopy invariant (Hatcher pp. 212–214). Refutes the World 2 claim.

stages.name: Same Holes
stages.description: Confirm the meters match.

stages.name: Cast on the Torus
stages.description: a ⌣ b lights the top class.

stages.name: Cast on the Bouquet
stages.description: a ⌣ b is dark: the loops never meet in a surface.

stages.name: Null's Answer
stages.description: Present the proof; the false island crumbles.

enemies.name: Mirror spawn
enemies.description: From 0-3: tries to make the islands look identical.

enemies.name: The Commutator (cameo)
enemies.description: Watches, then slips away toward the Station.

3-4.music: Gardens theme, then Null's motif dissolving when the top lantern lights.
3-4.visuals: Two islands side by side: a torus island and a bouquet of two loops attached to a sphere island; on the torus a third bright lantern lights where two beams cross; on the other, the beams pass without meeting.

3-5.site: Product Parterre — a formal garden laid out as a grid, each bed the product of a row and a column.
3-5.story: The cohomology of a product is built from its factors: rows times columns. The torus is a circle times a circle (1-5), and its lanterns are products of the circles' lanterns.
mechanics: Row and column beds hold each factor's lanterns; a bed lights with their cross product.
Künneth: for nice coefficients, the product's lanterns are exactly the bed products.
3-5.math_check: Cross product and the Künneth formula H*(X × Y; R) ≅ H*(X; R) ⊗ H*(Y; R) for H*(Y; R) free and finitely generated (Hatcher pp. 214–220).

stages.name: Row Times Column
stages.description: Circle times circle: four beds.

stages.name: Sphere Times Sphere
stages.description: S² × S²: lanterns in degrees 0, 2, 2, 4.

stages.name: Torsion in the Soil
stages.description: With torsion factors, the formula needs care; switch to field coefficients.

stages.name: Design a Parterre
stages.description: Lay out the beds for a triple product.

3-5.tools: Uses the Cup Caster and Suspension Sling.
3-5.music: Gardens theme as a minuet in strict rows.
3-5.visuals: A formal grid garden with lantern beds at row-column crossings; gold beams along rows and columns meeting in beds.

3-6.site: Polynomial Garden — a garden of nested lantern rings: one lantern, its square, its cube, until the top.
3-6.story: On projective spaces, one lantern generates everything: its powers light the whole garden until they reach the top. With this, Borsuk–Ulam returns in every dimension.
3-6.objective: Compute truncated polynomial rings and prove Borsuk–Ulam.
mechanics: Power steps: cup a lantern with itself repeatedly; each power lights the next ring.
RPⁿ with ℤ₂: the powers of α light rings 0..n; αⁿ⁺¹ = 0. CPⁿ with ℤ: powers of a degree-2 class.
Borsuk–Ulam: a map commuting with antipodes would force αⁿ⁺¹ ≠ 0 in a smaller garden — impossible.
3-6.math_check: H*(RPⁿ; ℤ₂) ≅ ℤ₂[α]/(αⁿ⁺¹), H*(CPⁿ; ℤ) ≅ ℤ[α]/(αⁿ⁺¹); Borsuk–Ulam (Hatcher pp. 220–229).

stages.name: Square It
stages.description: On RP², α ⌣ α lights the top.

stages.name: Climb the Powers
stages.description: Light RP³ and CP² ring by ring.

stages.name: Stops at the Top
stages.description: One more power: dark.

stages.name: Antipodes
stages.description: Find matching antipodal stations on a sphere — then prove they must exist.

3-6.music: Gardens theme as a round that adds a voice per power and stops abruptly at the top.
3-6.visuals: Concentric rings of lanterns rising like a tiered fountain, each tier brighter, the top tier crowned; a sphere island with paired opposite stations.

3-7.site: Compass Cliffs — sea cliffs on Poincaré Reach where small compasses spin at every point.
3-7.story: A place is orientable if compasses can be set consistently everywhere. Every place has an orientation double cover — two sheets, one for each choice (1-8) — and it is connected exactly when the place can't be oriented.
3-7.objective: Set local orientations and build the orientation double cover.
mechanics: Local compass: at each point, choose one of two orientations (a local homology generator).
Carry the compass along paths; returning flipped means non-orientable.
Sheet Compass: the two choices make a two-sheet cover; on a Möbius cliff it is one connected strip.
3-7.math_check: Local homology Hₙ(M, M − x) ≅ ℤ, orientations, the orientation double cover (Hatcher pp. 233–239).

stages.name: Set the Compasses
stages.description: Orient a torus cliff consistently.

stages.name: The Flip
stages.description: Walk a Möbius cliff; the compass returns flipped.

stages.name: Two Sheets
stages.description: Build the orientation double cover; it's connected on the Klein cliff.

stages.name: Survey
stages.description: Sort cliffs by orientability.

3-7.music: Poincaré Reach theme: a broad 88 bpm seascape in D major, horns and harp — first statement.
3-7.visuals: Tall sea cliffs on a reach of coast; small gold compasses spinning on posts; a cliff path twisting like a Möbius band.

3-8.site: The Seam — a glowing seam down Poincaré Reach where the land mirrors itself; every tower on one side has a twin on the other.
3-8.story: On a closed oriented manifold, holes in dimension k match readings in dimension n − k. Every tower has a twin across the seam. Without orientation, the match still works mod 2.
3-8.objective: Pair holes with readings across the seam (Poincaré duality).
mechanics: Dual cells: each k-cell has a dual (n−k)-cell crossing it once.
Seam mirror: holes on one side light their dual readings on the other.
Non-orientable: switch to ℤ₂ readings to restore the mirror.
3-8.math_check: Poincaré duality Hᵏ(M; ℤ) ≅ Hₙ₋ₖ(M; ℤ) for closed orientable n-manifolds; with ℤ₂ for all closed manifolds; dual cell decompositions as intuition (Hatcher pp. 239–249).

stages.name: Twin Towers
stages.description: Torus: H¹ pairs with H₁.

stages.name: Dual Cells
stages.description: Draw dual cells on a surface.

stages.name: Broken Mirror
stages.description: On the Klein bottle the integer mirror fails; ℤ₂ fixes it.

stages.name: Across the Seam
stages.description: Predict a 3-manifold's homology from half of it.

enemies.name: Seam wraith
enemies.description: New: tears the seam; three lashes.

3-8.tools: Uses the Cup Caster and Sheet Compass.
3-8.music: Poincaré Reach theme, its melody mirrored (inverted) in the bass.
3-8.visuals: A long coast split by a glowing seam; towers on one side with identical twins mirrored on the other; dual grids overlapping.

3-9.site: Pairing Pier — a pier where lanterns from opposite sides are paired across the water.
3-9.story: Duality and cup products together: every lantern has a partner whose product is the top lantern. CP² and S² ∨ S⁴ have the same holes, but only CP²'s middle lantern squares to the top.
3-9.objective: Use the cup pairing to tell CP² from S² ∨ S⁴.
mechanics: Pair lanterns across the pier; the pairing is perfect (nondegenerate) on a closed orientable manifold.
Square the middle lantern: on CP² it lights the top; on S² ∨ S⁴ it's dark — and S² ∨ S⁴ is not a manifold.
3-9.math_check: The cup product pairing is nondegenerate mod torsion for closed orientable manifolds; H*(CP²) vs H*(S² ∨ S⁴) (Hatcher pp. 249–252).

stages.name: Partners
stages.description: Pair torus lanterns.

stages.name: The Middle Lantern
stages.description: Square it on CP² and on S² ∨ S⁴.

3-9.music: Poincaré Reach theme and the Gardens theme played together.
3-9.visuals: A long stone pier at night with lanterns on both sides paired by gold beams across the water.

castle.site: The Counterfeit Station — a rail station at the end of Poincaré Reach with a perfect torus façade; behind it, a different place.
castle.story: The Commutator, now in disguise, runs a station that matches the torus group for group. Gyroid unmasks it with a cup product, polynomial powers and duality. Null retreats up his Spire into higher homotopy.

phases.name: The façade
phases.description: The station reads like a torus on every meter. Cast a ⌣ b: the top lantern stays dark. Tests 3-4.

phases.name: False powers
phases.description: The Commutator projects a fake projective space; climb its powers and find where they stop too early. Tests 3-6.

phases.name: No twin
phases.description: A tower without a twin across the seam: no duality, so not a closed manifold. Tests 3-8. The disguise falls.

enemies.name: The Commutator
enemies.description: Boss, disguised as a station master.

castle.tools: Cup Caster, Sheet Compass, reading wand.
castle.music: A sly 3/4 version of the Commutator's fugue on station chimes; the Gardens theme returns in full when the disguise falls.
castle.visuals: A grand rail station with a torus-shaped façade; behind it, a bouquet and sphere structure; lantern beams crossing the platforms.
castle.movie: castle-3-intro “The Counterfeit Station” and castle-3-outro “Up the Spire”.

3-1.scene: Level 'Reverse Engineering' at the Mirror Pools: twilight gardens with blue-gray stone paths and still mirror pools that reflect the paths; glowing gold values hover over path edges, and their reflections in the pools show arrows pointing the opposite way. Gyroid holds a slim gold wand. A violet reflection of a figure moves inside a pool.

3-2.scene: Level 'Torsion Shift' at the Torsion Terrace: stacked stone garden terraces at twilight; twisted glowing gold vines climb from each terrace up to the next. Gyroid climbs beside a vine. A violet vine strangles one.

3-3.scene: Level 'Front Face, Back Face' in the Lantern Rows: rows of tall stone lantern posts at twilight; two gold lantern beams cross and pool into a brighter third lantern. Gyroid holds up a glowing gold chalice that the beams pour into. Violet moths swarm around one lantern.

3-4.scene: Level 'A Cup of Counterexample' at the Twin Islands: two islands side by side at twilight — one shaped like a torus, the other made of two ring-shaped islands joined to a round dome-shaped sphere island. On the torus, two gold beams meet and a bright lantern lights at their crossing; on the other island the beams pass without meeting. Gyroid stands between them with a gold chalice; the Commutator watches from a boat.

3-5.scene: Level 'Product Placement' in the Product Parterre: a formal grid garden with hedge beds at row-column crossings; gold beams run along rows and columns and light lanterns where they meet. Gyroid walks a row. Violet moths flutter.

3-6.scene: Level 'Polynomial Garden': concentric tiers of lantern rings rising like a tiered fountain, each tier brighter gold than the last, the top tier crowned with light; beside it a small sphere island with two opposite stations glowing. Gyroid climbs the tiers.

3-7.scene: Level 'Which Way Is Up' at the Compass Cliffs: tall sea cliffs on a long coast at twilight; small gold compasses spin on posts along a cliff path that twists like a Möbius band. Gyroid holds a glowing compass. A violet frog flips a compass.

3-8.scene: Level 'Both Sides of the Story' at the Seam: a long coastline split down the middle by a glowing gold seam; stone towers on one side have identical mirrored twin towers on the other; a faint grid and its dual grid overlap across the land. Gyroid stands on the seam. A violet wraith tears at the seam.

3-9.scene: Level 'Perfect Pairing' at Pairing Pier: a long stone pier at night with lanterns along both sides, each paired with one opposite by a gold beam across the water. Gyroid and Emmy Boundary walk the pier.

castle_art.scene: Castle 'The Counterfeit Station': a grand stone rail station at night whose front façade is shaped like a perfect torus, but seen from the side its back is a bouquet of two rings attached to a dome — a fake. Lantern beams cross the platforms. The Commutator (from the reference) in a station master's cloak over his loop-pauldron armor, mask half-raised. Gyroid confronts him holding a glowing gold chalice; Emmy Boundary beside him.

videos.title: Into the Cup Product Gardens
videos.plays: After castle-2 (The Retractor), before World 3 · Level 1
videos.synopsis: Null's ball-to-boundary retractor failed (H₂(B³) = 0 — Brouwer one dimension up). The Commutator shows up in disguise at a counterfeit station that matches the torus group for group. Gyroid enters the signal gardens, where cochains read chains backwards and classes multiply. Null's new claim: every map S³ → S² is trivial.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: The two choices make a cover — the Sheet Compass sees it.

videos.title: Both Sides of the Story
videos.plays: Before World 3 · Level 8, at the Seam
videos.synopsis: Across the Seam every tower has a twin: holes in dimension k match readings in dimension n − k.

scenes.title: The Seam
scenes.description: A glowing seam runs down the coast; towers mirror across it.

scenes.title: Twins
scenes.description: A tower lights on one side; its twin lights on the other.

scenes.title: Wraith
scenes.description: A violet wraith claws at the seam.

scenes.title: Ready
scenes.description: Gyroid steps onto the seam.

scenes.title: Title
scenes.description: Title card at 26: “World 3 · Level 8 — Both Sides of the Story”.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: On a closed, oriented place, every hole has a twin reading on the other side.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: Dimension k on this side, n minus k on that one.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: If the place is twisted, count mod 2 and the mirror still works.

videos.title: Perfect Pairing
videos.plays: Before World 3 · Level 9, at Pairing Pier
videos.synopsis: Every lantern has a partner whose product is the top. CP²'s middle lantern squares to the top; S² ∨ S⁴'s doesn't.

scenes.title: The pier
scenes.description: Lanterns paired across the water by beams.

scenes.title: The middle lantern
scenes.description: Gyroid squares the middle lantern of two models: one blazes, one stays dark.

scenes.title: The station
scenes.description: The Counterfeit Station's lights in the distance.

scenes.title: Title
scenes.description: Title card at 22: “World 3 · Level 9 — Perfect Pairing”.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: On a closed manifold, every lantern has a partner. Their product is the top.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: Same holes — but only one middle lantern squares to the top.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: Time to visit that station.

videos.title: The Counterfeit Station
videos.synopsis: A station with a perfect torus façade, matching every hole count. Its masked station master knows Gyroid's name.

scenes.title: The façade
scenes.description: A grand station shaped like a torus; meters on its walls read like a torus.

scenes.title: The master
scenes.description: The station master steps out; under his cloak, loop pauldrons.

scenes.title: Unmasked
scenes.description: He throws back the cloak: the Commutator.

scenes.title: Title
scenes.description: Title card at 26: “World 3 · Castle — The Counterfeit Station”.

captions.speaker: The Commutator
captions.text: Welcome to the torus, courier. Count my holes — you'll find them all in order.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: The Commutator. You don't give up.

captions.speaker: The Commutator
captions.text: Your counting forgot order once. It will forget again.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: We don't just count anymore. We multiply.

videos.title: Up the Spire
videos.plays: After castle-3 — the end of World 3
videos.synopsis: The façade falls; the Commutator escapes again. Null retreats up the Postnikov Spire, where rooms unfold into higher dimensions and his Crown waits.

scenes.title: The façade falls
scenes.description: The torus façade cracks and falls away, revealing two rings and a dome.

scenes.title: Escape
scenes.description: The Commutator leaps onto a departing train of violet light.

scenes.title: The Spire
scenes.description: On the horizon a tower rises into the clouds, each floor a room that unfolds into more dimensions; at the top, the Null Crown's violet glow.

scenes.title: World 3 complete
scenes.description: Card: “World 3 complete — Cup Product Gardens restored.”

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: No top lantern, no twin across the seam. Your station was never a torus.

captions.speaker: The Commutator
captions.text: Then I'll find somewhere your lanterns can't reach.

captions.speaker: Count Null
captions.text: Climb my Spire, courier. Up here, shapes have more than holes.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: Then we climb. Every floor.
